breaks.quote: And it doesn’t start from zero. Somewhere in your life, you have already changed something without noticing.
breaks.why: The closing lines drop in new ideas with no example, reason or step, so the reader is left holding claims they cannot use.

breaks.quote: Lasting Change works with the part of you that wants to stay the same, one step at a time, in an order it can accept.
breaks.why: The idea is named and asserted but never shown, so the reader cannot picture what working with that part looks like.

breaks.quote: Because it is not finished with you. It still has a lesson to teach, and you have not learned it yet. Regret is not punishment, it is there to stop you repeating something.
breaks.why: A surprising claim about regret is stated flat with no example, reason or premise, so the reader must take it on trust.

breaks.quote: And when you cannot answer, tell it as a story about somebody else and find the moral.
breaks.why: A new technique is handed over with no reason or step, and the jump from chimpanzees to the reader's own regret is not bridged.

breaks.quote: He tried out his opening line on his morning customers. Before December, he was confident.
breaks.why: Steps are missing between avoiding his own voice and being confident, so the reader has to guess how the change happened.
